History:
- Presenting complaint: dysuria, urinary frequency, lower abdominal ache, and noted pink-tinged urine today.
- Onset/duration/progression: symptoms present for just under one week; dysuria and increased frequency noted throughout; pink discoloration of urine noticed today.
- Symptom context/triggers: lower abdominal ache worse with urination; no flank or back pain.
- Associated symptoms: denies fever, nausea, vomiting; denies unusual vaginal discharge.
- Sexual/reproductive history: sexually active with long-term boyfriend; reports not using condoms; on combined oral contraceptive pill; last unprotected sex approximately 1 week ago; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Bowel history: history of IBS with variable bowel habits, no change from baseline.
- Social: tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago (first time); occasional alcohol use; lives in university halls.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (patient-reported).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- Allergies: reaction to Clindamycin reported (reaction details not documented).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Medication for IBS (patient states name begins with "M", not fully documented) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical exam documented; clinician did not examine.
- Relevant negatives reported: no fever, no nausea/vomiting, no back or flank pain, no abnormal vaginal discharge reported.

Impression:
- Likely lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Management Plan:
- Antibiotic therapy discussed: Trimethoprim and Nitrofurantoin offered as options.
  - Trimethoprim — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Nitrofurantoin — described by clinician as a "three-day course"; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Urine sample advised and arranged: patient to attend practice to drop off a urine sample for point-of-care testing and send to laboratory for culture/sensitivity.
- Supportive measures: maintain good hydration; use simple analgesia (paracetamol) for pain.
- Safety-netting:
  - Return/seek review if symptoms do not improve within one week.
  - Contact clinician urgently if fever, back/flank pain, or vomiting develop.

Patient Summary:
- Amanda Jackson, 19, presents with ~1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency, lower abdominal aching, and recent pink urine. Findings are most consistent with an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis). Urine sample arranged and antibiotics (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin) discussed; supportive care and follow-up advised.

Key Takeaways:
- Provide a urine sample at the practice so it can be tested and sent to the lab.
- Start prescribed antibiotics (choice to be confirmed) and stay well hydrated.
- Return promptly or seek urgent care if fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting occur.

Next Steps:
- Patient to attend practice to provide a urine sample for dipstick and culture/sensitivity.
- Prescribe and initiate antibiotic treatment (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin) — specific agent/dose to be documented when prescribed.
- Follow-up if no clinical improvement within one week or sooner for worsening symptoms.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP), results of urine dipstick/urine culture, exact antibiotic chosen with dose/route/frequency, exact name and dosing of IBS medication, details of allergic reaction to Clindamycin.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: initial brief response "No" when asked about sexual activity followed by clarification that she is sexually active with a long-term boyfriend (clarified in transcript) — conflict noted but resolved by patient clarification.
- Transcript quality: generally clear and audible; occasional unclear medication name (IBS med) and antibiotic allergy name (Clindamycin) spelling/wording.
